title: Legal Intelligence
titleZh: LLM × 法律助手：产品生态与创业机会
subtitle: Evidence-first legal AI NDA review · Research, PRD and technical architecture
summary: Source-backed legal AI desk research, a scoped New York-law mutual NDA MVP specification, and proposed algorithm, backend and frontend architecture. Product implementation and PMF are not claimed.
summaryZh: 法律 AI 一手研究、纽约州法双向 NDA 产品规格，以及算法、后端、前端技术设计。产品仍未开发或验证。
problem: Business users and lawyers need to understand legal documents, locate consequential risks and produce reviewable work while minimizing hallucinations, privacy exposure and jurisdiction mistakes.
thesis: A jurisdiction-scoped contract review workbench with clause-level evidence, editable redlines, auditable review and human handoff may create more durable value than a generic AI lawyer chat interface. PMF is not established.
findings: Product Hunt feedback values draft acceleration and plain-language comprehension, but users still report edits, unclear scope, latency and onboarding friction.
Hacker News debate centers on authoritative case law access, professional judgment, data confidentiality, correct citations and enterprise workflow integration.
Product designs cluster around document drafting, consumer explanation, AI-plus-lawyer handoff, email-native legal agents, law-firm operations and jurisdiction-specific research.
A limited-jurisdiction NDA/SaaS contract-risk reviewer is a testable wedge, not validated demand or a legal quality guarantee.
risks: Small, nonrepresentative PH review samples and anonymous HN discourse cannot establish demand or adoption.
No product trials, paid conversion/retention measurement, legal accuracy benchmark or independent security audit were conducted.
Jurisdiction, license-to-practice, model hallucinations, confidentiality, privilege and source recency require specialist review.
No conclusions in this research should be used as legal advice.
The v1.0 PRD/MVP documents are design specifications only; no product implementation, security certification or legal performance benchmark is claimed.
method: Desk research of original Product Hunt launch/review pages (nine representative products) and Hacker News threads, cross-checked against Stanford HAI's 2024 study, ABA Formal Opinion 512 and vendor documentation. Evidence grades distinguish independent findings, first-person comments, discussion opinions and promotional claims.
